ahn-div-134-n34.summary: Eight weeks before the battle of Salamanca, Marshal Jourdan, King Joseph’s chief of staff, orders Soult to reinforce Count d’Erlon’s corps against General Hill, or to send it across the Tagus at the bridge of the Arzobispo if Wellington calls Hill back to him. The letter was intercepted: a contemporary Spanish translation survives in the Archivo Histórico Nacional, with the enciphered passages left as numbers, undeciphered. They read with the table of the 1812 Grand Chiffre.
ahn-div-134-n34.en: [Madrid, 28 May 1812. To Marshal the Duke of Dalmatia. Monsieur le Maréchal, the King has just received a letter from Marshal the Duke of Ragusa dated the 26th. This marshal states positively that Lord Wellington is north of the Tagus with his whole army, except Hill’s division. He takes it as certain that around the 8th the whole English army will have moved against him. Two divisions have already crossed the Douro, etc. He is continuing towards Zamora in order to support the army of Galicia, which was preparing to advance.] The Duke of Ragusa has recalled Foy’s division to him, so that there will remain in the Tagus valley only three battalions and about eight hundred horse of the Army of the Centre, under the orders of General Treillard.

ahn-div-134-n73.en:
DRAFT made at write-up (27 Oct 2026) from Brice Dudout's French working notes readingN73partial.md; not part of the
contributed text. Only the cipher passages and the clear phrases quoted around them in the notes are translated.
Conventions as in the notes: {x} probable reading; ‹…› unresolved; [x] restored from the sense; (clear) = a clear phrase
of the copy, as quoted in the notes.

(clear) "The rule from which I will not depart is this."

A1: It is that only an absolute certainty and ca{pi}tal operations begun in [the] South can outweigh the pro‹…›ties
[probabilities?] of an operation in the North;

(clear) "and I base myself in this on"

A2: the ‹…› parti‹…›{cu}lar [situation?] which is impo‹…› [imposed?] on me, and the difference, for the enemy, of a success

(clear) "on one side or the other"

A3: a success whose effects ‹…› [cannot?] be com‹…›pa‹…›red.

system: Grand Chiffre of 1812 (the British “Great Paris Cipher”): a repertory of 1,200 numbers (letters, syllables, words) extended to 1,400 with additions for Spain (1211 = the Army of the Centre, 1214 = the English army, 1300 = Lord Wellington, 1383 = the Tagus);…
